profile.reading:
OVHcloud Hillsboro is one of two data centers that anchored OVHcloud's entry into the United States market, located at 1300 Northeast 25th Avenue in Hillsboro, Oregon, inside the Portland area technology corridor often called the Silicon Forest that also hosts major semiconductor and networking operations. OVHcloud is a French cloud and hosting company, one of Europe's largest, that builds and operates the great majority of its own data centers and designs much of its own server hardware rather than buying capacity from third party colocation providers. The Hillsboro facility opened in 2018, alongside a sister site in Vint Hill, Virginia that gave OVHcloud its first US East and US West presence, and the company marked both sites' fifth anniversary with a public announcement in 2023.

OVHcloud has publicly described the technology inside its US data centers, including this one, as built around a proprietary water cooling system rather than conventional air conditioning. The company states this approach helps it achieve some of the lowest power usage effectiveness ratings in the industry, since moving heat with water is markedly more efficient than cooling a data hall with chilled air. OVHcloud also promotes a vertically integrated model in which it designs, builds, operates and eventually recycles its own servers, extending hardware through a second or third operational life before disposal, a sustainability posture the company ties directly to facilities like Hillsboro.

Beyond that, OVHcloud has not published a power capacity figure in megawatts, a square footage or white space figure, or formal certifications specific to the Hillsboro building, and this entry does not estimate those numbers. As of the company's most recent public infrastructure count, Hillsboro sits among roughly three dozen OVHcloud data centers worldwide, spanning Europe, North America and Asia Pacific, used to host the company's public cloud, private cloud, dedicated server and web hosting product lines for customers across the Americas. Given OVHcloud's ownership model, capacity at this site is presumed to serve OVHcloud's own multi tenant customer base directly rather than a single anchor tenant, though the company does not publish a tenant list for any individual facility. No county permit or expansion filing specific to this address has been reviewed for this entry.

sources.title: OVHcloud US Celebrates Five-Year Anniversary of Vint Hill and Hillsboro Data Centers

profile.research_note: OVHcloud's own 5-year-anniversary press release (published 2023) dates this Hillsboro facility to ~2018; describes proprietary water-cooling but publishes no MW/sqft/certification figures.

reading.body:
OVHcloud's Hillsboro campus has no published IT load, power capacity, or rack count in the operator's specifications. The facility is mapped at 1300 NE 25th Avenue in Hillsboro, Oregon, but the operator has not released performance metrics that would indicate its role in AI infrastructure scaling.

Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities, but only 8 publish power capacity figures. Those eight facilities together account for 156.6 MW of published capacity. OVHcloud Hillsboro does not appear in the eight published figures, which means it either publishes no capacity data or publishes capacity below the threshold of sites this project has indexed.

Without published specifications, this campus cannot be ranked against peers or assessed for its bearing on regional AI compute availability. The absence of public capacity data is itself a fact: most data centers, even in a state with substantial mapped inventory, do not disclose the figures needed to gauge their role in AI scaling constraints.
